stories.title: DOJ accuses Southern Poverty Law Center of using donations to pay secret informants
stories.summary: The Justice Department has accused the Southern Poverty Law Center of money laundering and other crimes. The DOJ says the Alabama-based civil rights organization paid sources to stoke racial hatred.

stories.title: A former South Korean spy confronts the hidden war that never ended
stories.summary: More than 70 years after the Korean War, South Korea is still confronting the legacy of a secret conflict waged in the shadows.

stories.title: Knitting enthusiasts from around the country recently met for yarn fest
stories.summary: People who love to knit held a convention recently where they showed off their love for yarn and fiber arts.

stories.title: Small, inexpensive drones are changing the battlefield. The Pentagon is playing catchup
stories.summary: As small attack drones become central to warfare, the Pentagon is making a major push to jumpstart manufacturing.

stories.title: Amid a ceasefire in Lebanon, one family buries their daughter
stories.summary: Last week, NPR spent time with a family still searching for their 26-year-old daughter in the rubble one week after Israeli airstrikes hit Beirut. Now her remains have been identified.

stories.title: More immigrants are being held in detention for over a year. NPR followed one family's ordeal.
stories.summary: The El Gamal family has been held in ICE detention for more than 320 days. They are not alone: the number of immigrants who've been in ICE detention for over a year has skyrocketed.
